provenance.source: Lindert & Williamson, 'American Incomes 1774-1860', NBER WP 18396 (2012); extended in 'Unequal Gains: American Growth and Inequality since 1700' (Princeton, 2016)
provenance.extracted: transcribed from the paper's Tables 6-7 and the summary passage (sec. IV); exact-stated figures quoted in-text
provenance.note: Pre-1913 US income inequality, read straight as a set fact. It sits BEHIND the WID top-1% floor (1913) used in sec 3d, carrying the pyramid back through the antebellum rise. Geography labelled per row; slaves-in/out labelled. No imported null.

bridge_to_wid: WID US top-1% before-tax share picks up at 1913 (~18%), peaks 22.3% in 1928 (sec 3d). LW shows the climb already underway 1774->1860 (top-1% ~7->10%), so the current pyramid's rise is continuous with the antebellum one, not born at 1913.
